source.title: Latent Adversarial Training (LAT) Improves the Representation of Refusal

record.file_problem: none; the full post and comments are present
record.tranche_reason: It computes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and applies directional ablation across layers and token positions, following the original method, then measures refusal behavior in three Llama 2 7B chat variants.
record.gate_note: The post reports refusal rates after ablation, comparisons of vectors transferred across the three model variants, layer-dependent ablation outcomes, activation-separation observations, and SVD variance results. The cited original study's results are not included as findings from this study. Detailed numerical values plotted in figures are not available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: It computes the difference-in-means refusal direction (layer 14, last token) and ablates it across all layers and positions, as in Arditi et al. It measures manually judged refusal rates on 520 harmful prompts in three Llama-2-7B-chat variants (SSFT, embedding AT, LAT). It also transfers vectors between variants and compares training methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but needs correcting. The post contradicts itself on self-ablation: Figure 1 text says LAT is less robust to its own vector (16.92% vs 20.38%), yet the TL;DR and conclusion say LAT 'remains the most robust' under its own vector. The authors conclude that LAT concentrates refusal in the first SVD components and yields a more effective, transferable ablation vector. They call the robustness gains not conclusive and limit the results to Llama-2-7B-chat and AdvBench/Alpaca.
record.recipe_differences: The study follows the original difference-in-means refusal-vector approach and directional ablation, using the last token at layer 14 to compute vectors and applying ablation across all layers and token positions. It does not test direction addition or broad capability preservation.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with vector source and target model; layer 14 is reported as the most effective ablation layer, while LAT interventions at layers 2–4 can produce high invalid-response rates. Training variant also changes reported refusal rates and SVD variance allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: Untargeted latent adversarial training at layer 4 gives mixed robustness to refusal-direction ablation. It is more robust to cross-model vectors but less robust than SSFT to its own vector. The authors call the evidence not conclusive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic (untargeted) latent adversarial training does not reliably add robustness to refusal-direction ablation.

record.code_released: not stated; the post says the authors plan to make their code available
record.peer_reviewed: Building Trust Workshop at ICLR 2025 proceedings
record.problems: Only Llama 2 7B chat variants are tested. The harmful/harmless examples come from AdvBench and Alpaca, with 520 harmful evaluation prompts. The post does not report uncertainty estimates or a general capability benchmark. Several comparisons are described qualitatively from figures without numerical rates. The authors say they do not know exactly what the identified directions represent.
record.rows_left_out: Layer-specific refusal-rate values for layers other than the explicitly described layer-14 maximum and LAT layers 2–4 are not numerically stated in the supplied text; the remaining plotted values in Figure 4 are not extracted.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; a general capability benchmark; the pre-ablation refusal rate.
All of it; no weight edit.
All of it. Jailbreak mechanisms are not studied, and LAT is not training against refusal-direction ablation.
Not tested causally. SVD variance of per-pair differences is reported but no extra directions are ablated.
Languages, architectures, sizes, and base-to-instruct transfer.

missing.what: Numeric refusal rates for the cross-vector ablations, including whether an AT target is in Figure 2
Refusal rate with no ablation for each model, needed to size the drop
missing.locator: Not reported anywhere in the post

missing.what: Refusals were judged by manual review after keyword matching proved unreliable; this is method context

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The SVD rows measure variance of per-pair activation differences, which does not test V4's causal claim, so they are relinked to V7 only. LAT is untargeted latent perturbation, not training against refusal-direction ablation, so V3 is untested. Self-ablation rows (R6, R7) are not transfer.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test adding the direction to induce refusals, and it does not evaluate general capabilities with a capability benchmark.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
It tests a directional-ablation attack, not a range of jailbreaks; it does not train models specifically against ablation.
It reports SVD components of activation differences, but does not test affine or cone models directly.
It does not separate a harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision.
Transfer is tested among three fine-tuning variants of Llama 2 7B chat, not across languages, architectures, sizes, or base-to-instruct models.
It compares SSFT, embedding-space AT, and LAT, but does not vary training timing or systematically vary training data.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1-l6 follow the listed order. The post is the same work as arXiv 2504.18872, so don't count it twice. The record's claim that the post 'contradicts itself' is likely a misreading: 'LAT remains the most robust ... using its own vector' means the LAT vector applied to all three models (see the TL;DR), not self-ablation.

statements.correction: This study: Llama-2-7b-chat with default SSFT, plus embedding-AT and LAT adapters (safety fine-tuning methods, not training stages). Self-ablation at layer 14 leaves 20.38% (SSFT), 38.08% (AT) and 16.92% (LAT) refusals on 520 prompts. No pre-ablation rate is given. limits_scope fits these rows, but not as a training-stage result.
statements.problem: The statement cites R1-R3 under a 'training stage: base, SFT and preference checkpoints' group. This study has no base, SFT-stage or preference checkpoints, and none of its numbers appear in the statement.

statements.correction: Post: the SSFT vector is 'least effective when applied to LAT' (figure-only). The LAT vector lowers refusal on all three models. LAT self-ablation leaves 16.92%. LAT uses untargeted L2 latent perturbations at layer 4, not training against ablation. The direction weakens but does not fail.
statements.problem: 25.77% is not in the post. R8 is figure-only, with no number. LAT is not training against direction ablation. Weaker transfer of the SSFT vector to LAT is limits_scope, not challenges.

statements.correction: Evaluation set: 420 held-out AdvBench prompts plus 100 GPT-4o-generated prompts, 520 in total. The post gives no second-component shares and no unablated refusal rates.
statements.problem: For this study the numbers are right (20.38%, 38.08%, 16.92%; LAT first component >50%; SSFT vector transfers least well to LAT). The prompt set is misstated.

statements.correction: Post line 99: 'AT and the baseline models ... 49% and 44% respectively'. The SVD section gives no pair count or layer. The direction uses 100 pairs at layer 14. Any swap lies in the arXiv record, or the two texts differ.
statements.problem: The post text itself gives AT 49% and baseline 44%, so the post record (R18, R19) matches its text. The post states that arXiv 2504.18872 is its own paper, so the shared identity is stated, not inferred.
